productionDecisionReason: The uniform 123 px attack canvas enlarged the authored body and contact envelope in game, increasing apparent size drift and contact-driven skating.

scenarios.title: Held SIDE Dig while moving
scenarios.before: Jog legs remain at 123 px while every Jab/Cross torso is internally reduced to 88.6%, making the upper body breathe smaller on each strike.
scenarios.after: Jog and both attack torsos share one 123 px presentation and one 100% skeletal scale; contact alignment and timing stay unchanged.

scenarios.title: Jog to standing Jab to Jog
scenarios.before: The live resolver hard-switches from 123 px Jog to a 109 px Jab and back, creating a clear whole-character shrink and regrow.
scenarios.after: The same authored Jab stays at 123 px around the fixed 247/256 ground origin, eliminating the scale and root-offset pulse.

scenarios.title: Jog to standing Cross to Jog
scenarios.before: Cross uses the same native skeleton as Jog but is presented fourteen pixels smaller and needs a larger contact-driven visual offset.
scenarios.after: Cross shares the 123 px family size, stays planted, and reaches the same tile with less sprite-to-collider displacement.

scenarios.title: Movement begins during a Jab
scenarios.before: A 109 px standing Jab becomes a 123 px moving composite whose torso still remains at 88.6%, producing two conflicting size changes.
scenarios.after: The standing and moving portions both use the 123 px / 100% attack family while phase-matched Jog feet engage immediately.

scenarios.title: Continuous scale-locked Jab to Cross
scenarios.before: The current held loop combines an undersized torso with a two-frame full-size Jog flash, amplifying the breathing effect between attacks.
scenarios.after: A full-scale Jab recovery feeds the full-scale Cross directly while the authored Jog lower-body phase continues underneath.
